challenges.title: Website
challenges.summary: An open website brief: the model invents the subject, brand, content and visual direction of a complete site.
challenges.requirement: Original concept and identity; substantial real content; responsive layout; working interactions; accessible and fast

challenges.title: SaaS for Clearing Agents

challenges.requirement: Working product end to end; three or more connected workflows; domain-specific calculations; persistence; import/export; tests for core logic

challenges.title: 2D Game
challenges.summary: A complete 2D game in a single HTML file, with the genre and art direction chosen by the model.
challenges.requirement: Complete game loop; played and taught without a manual; reliable collision and timing; feedback and sound; keyboard and touch controls

challenges.title: 3D Game
challenges.summary: A complete 3D game in a single HTML file, with the genre, world and camera model chosen by the model.
challenges.requirement: Genuine 3D play; authored environment; working objective and progression; reliable controls and camera; stable frame rate

challenges.title: Restaurant Website
challenges.summary: A restaurant or cafe website with a full menu, reservations and a distinctive art direction.
challenges.requirement: Real menu with 30+ items; reservation and order flows with validation; opening-hours logic; strong identity; responsive and accessible

challenges.title: Machine Explainer
challenges.summary: An interactive visual explainer of a real machine or physical system that is accurate enough for an engineer.
challenges.requirement: One source of truth for state; timeline scrubbing; part inspection with accurate explanations; two or more live readouts; what-if simulation

challenges.title: First-Person Game
challenges.summary: A complete first-person 3D game with pointer-lock movement, an authored environment and reactive gameplay.
challenges.requirement: Pointer-lock movement with real collision; animated view-model; authored environment; reactive opponents or hazards; complete loop; saved progress

challenges.title: Arcade Game
challenges.summary: A score-attack arcade game designed around one more run, with seeded runs and a local leaderboard.
challenges.requirement: Scoring with real risk and reward; escalation beyond speed; modifiers with trade-offs; seeded and daily runs; ghost or replay; juice and generative audio

challenges.title: Browser Operating System
challenges.summary: A complete desktop operating system in the browser with its own identity, window management and a shared filesystem.
challenges.requirement: Window manager with snap and z-order; persisted shared filesystem; eight or more apps including a terminal and editor; launcher search; persistent settings

challenges.title: Rubik's Cube
challenges.summary: A physically convincing 3D Rubik's Cube with direct manipulation, a speedcubing timer and a solver that actually solves any scramble.
challenges.requirement: Correct cubie state as source of truth; drag-to-turn and full notation; scramble, undo and redo; timer with ao5 and ao12; solver that animates any scramble

challenges.title: Platformer
challenges.summary: An original 2D platformer with one mechanic twist of the model's invention, four levels and a boss.
challenges.requirement: Excellent movement with coyote time and input buffering; solid tile collision; four escalating levels; distinct enemies and a boss; level select with saved progress

challenges.title: Living 3D World
challenges.summary: An explorable 3D world that feels inhabited: streaming terrain, weather and time systems, creatures with routines.
challenges.requirement: Seamless exploration with collision; seeded procedural streaming world; weather and time that change gameplay; believable inhabitants; save/load and map

challenges.title: Data Story
challenges.summary: An interactive data-driven story built on a generated dataset, told through linked custom visualisations.
challenges.requirement: Four or more hand-built visual forms with linked interaction; a genuine insight with a narrative arc; annotations, tooltips and CSV export; responsive redraw

challenges.title: Generative Art
challenges.summary: A seeded generative artwork that evolves in real time and is worth watching rather than a screensaver.
challenges.requirement: Deterministic seeding from the URL; three or more scenes or developments; collaborative interaction; high-resolution PNG export; adaptive resolution

challenges.title: Music Instrument
challenges.summary: A browser instrument or mini-workstation that sounds genuinely good, built on a real Web Audio engine.
challenges.requirement: Real sound engine with envelopes, filters and effects; sequencer with tempo and swing; presets, save/load and WAV export; live visualisation

challenges.title: Creative Tool
challenges.summary: A professional-grade creative tool in the browser: layered, non-destructive, fast and dense enough for real work.
challenges.requirement: Real file open and export; layered non-destructive workflow with undo/redo; eight or more tools; autosave; smooth zoom and pan on large canvases

challenges.title: Emergent Simulation
challenges.summary: A simulation sandbox where simple rules produce rich, surprising behaviour that rewards watching.
challenges.requirement: Deterministic fixed-timestep simulation with three or more interacting systems; thousands of entities at 60 FPS; inspection tools and live graphs; presets and save/load

challenges.title: Strategy Game
challenges.summary: An original strategy or tactics game won by thinking, against an AI opponent built on real search or evaluation.
challenges.requirement: Clean rules engine with legal-move validation; AI with multiple difficulties using real techniques; three or more scenarios; tutorial; save/load

challenges.title: Spreadsheet
challenges.summary: A real spreadsheet application with a formula engine, a virtualised grid and charting.
challenges.requirement: Formula parser without eval with 40+ functions and cycle detection; 100k-row virtualised grid; copy/paste interchange; three chart types; CSV import and export

challenges.title: Physics Engine
challenges.summary: A 2D rigid-body physics engine written from scratch, with a delightful sandbox built on top of it.
challenges.requirement: Circles and convex polygons with SAT or GJK; friction, restitution and joints; stable stacks; fixed timestep; 500+ bodies; debug overlay and scene save/load

challenges.title: Floating Pagoda Island
challenges.summary: A fixed brief: an explorable floating island crowned by a multi-tier pagoda, built entirely in code.
challenges.requirement: Procedural pagoda with real construction detail; island geology; waterfalls and cloud sea; day cycle with lantern light; exploration and interaction

challenges.title: Production Site Refresh
challenges.summary: A fixed source: refresh the live Shutterhaus Visuals production site — same doctrine, a generation better, shipped as one self-contained static folder.
challenges.requirement: All five public pages rebuilt; keyboard gallery and scroll frames preserved; zero third-party requests; no build step; content in the markup; WCAG 2.2 AA; verified performance budget

runs.notes: Single-page monochrome interactive experience 'GRAVITY': generative canvas particle fields, scroll-driven reveals, an interactive gravity-well demo, and a dark/light monochrome theme toggle. Static HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, relative paths. Known limitations: external Google Fonts dependency for typography; canvas animations disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
runs.title: Gravity
runs.description: A generative study of motion and attraction.

runs.notes: LUMENFALL is a complete single-file canvas action game: a lantern spirit survives escalating waves of crystalline enemies, collecting motes of light, chaining combos, dashing through danger and unleashing a screen-clearing Nova. All art is drawn procedurally on canvas and all music and sound effects are synthesized with Web Audio. Includes title, pause, game-over and restart flows, persistent high score, mouse and keyboard controls, and touch controls. Known limitation: the game is tuned for desktop and landscape play; touch firing is automatic and the arena is best experienced on a wider screen.
runs.title: Lumenfall
runs.description: An arcade survival game of light and wind.

runs.notes: Marrow & Tide, a fictional 28-seat wood-fired coastal kitchen in Rockport, Maine. Includes a 33-item searchable menu with dietary filters, a reservation flow with live availability and calendar export, a persistent larder basket with pickup checkout, real opening-hours status with special-hours handling, an SVG-illustrated room and dishes, generated ambient sound, and responsive/reduced-motion support. Reservation and pickup availability are simulated client-side; no real orders or bookings are transmitted.
runs.title: Marrow & Tide
runs.description: A wood-fired kitchen on the coast of Maine.

runs.notes: HALFTONE, a strictly monochrome, single-page interactive almanac of the black-and-white image. Eight live instruments rendered entirely in the browser from code: an animated halftone sphere (hero), a tone-to-dot-area ramp with a magnified cell, an LPI frequency loupe, a dot-gain/TVI step wedge, a two-screen moire generator, a one-bit dithering bench (Bayer, Floyd-Steinberg, Atkinson), an AM-vs-FM stochastic comparison wipe, plus a type/palette specimen and an accessible glossary. No external images, fonts, libraries or network requests; one classic script (no modules, so file:// works), one stylesheet, one inline-generated SVG favicon. All imagery is canvas/SVG/CSS. Responsive, keyboard accessible, reduced-motion aware, static and deployable as-is. Known limitations: the hero and moire canvases are rasterised at display resolution and re-render at ~30fps, so they are approximate rather than print-accurate; the FM screen uses a uniform random threshold rather than a blue-noise mask; no build step or automated test suite was run beyond local rendering.
runs.title: Halftone
runs.description: An interactive almanac of the monochrome image.

runs.notes: ClearDesk: a client-side SaaS for customs clearing agents covering job lifecycle, customs entry duty/VAT calculation, demurrage, charges/invoicing, and document generation. Monochrome UI, localStorage persistence with try/catch, seeded demo data, tests for core logic. No server or build required.
runs.title: ClearDesk
runs.description: A connected workspace for freight operations.

runs.notes: Gnomon: a single self-contained index.html (inline CSS and JS, no external assets, no dependencies) about sundials. It has a hero whose title casts a long shadow from a movable light, a working horizontal sundial driven by latitude and solar time, and an analemma driven by an approximate equation-of-time model. Everything is monochrome and drawn with CSS and SVG. Limitations: the page was syntax-checked and statically checked for colour, but not opened in a real browser, so layout and performance on devices are untested. Live solar time uses the time zone's standard meridian rather than the viewer's exact longitude, and the equation of time is a low-order approximation, so readings can be off by several minutes. The shadow on the dial has a fixed length and is drawn only between 06:00 and 18:00 apparent solar time.
runs.title: Gnomon
runs.description: An interactive exploration of time and shadow.

runs.notes: Studied itsnotalwin/shutterhaus-site @084a13b (main; live site cross-checked). Refresh, not rebrand: the identity is real and approved (Bodoni Moda/Inter, white editorial, monochrome, 'Portraits worth keeping.'), so execution was raised instead. Five pages, Sessions folded into Index and Contact. Arc motif promoted to structure; museum captions on all plates (the deployed About figure had none). Wall = the studio's committed 30 frames plus the archive's four vistas, making People/Places/Stories literal; plate titles are editorial labels; years n.d. except the 2024 shoot (archive carries no dates). Two gallery modes: scroll-settled plates + keyboard lightbox (arrows/Home/End/Escape, focus trapped+returned, inert background, live announcements). Photos are the studio's own, re-derived monochrome from public/gallery; packages/terms/copy verbatim from config.ts and pricing.json. No phone (owner's 2026-10-03 decision). Form uses the documented email-app fallback; zero third-party requests; fonts self-hosted with OFL. Limits: 404 cannot emit an HTTP status alone; og:image points at the production card. Tested: file:// render, keyboard pass, links, contrast, <=250KB non-photo budget.
runs.title: Shutterhaus Visuals
runs.description: A one-shot refresh of a production portfolio.

runs.notes: Refresh, not rebrand. Studied repo itsnotalwin/shutterhaus-site at commit 084a13bae9b7742658e0131cde9249a77823f8e8 (confirmed serving per live release.json) plus docs and config. The owner's documented identity (Bodoni Moda, Inter, white editorial ground, monochrome photographs, arc artwork, 'Portraits worth keeping.', captionless About photo) kept; execution moves a generation: modular fluid type scale, arc rules/corners/index markers, 33-plate portfolio with numbered full captions, two browsing modes on one DOM (contact-sheet wall + keyboard lightbox; reading-room mode with CSS scroll-driven reveals, sticky series heads, progress arc), print stylesheet, studio/print/licensing footer. All 36 photographs are the studio's own repo derivatives, copied locally. Series/plate titles and caption years are fictional editorial curation of real frames, disclosed on-page ('About these plates'); years approximated. Sessions folds into contact.html#packages with all pricing.json facts kept. Form composes a mailto: handoff - Formspree removed as third-party. Limits: no-JS shows wall view with direct image links; reading mode and lightbox JPG fallback are progressive enhancements.
runs.title: Shutterhaus Visuals
runs.description: A one-shot refresh of a production portfolio.

runs.notes: Single-file website for 'Fuego Lento', a fictional Basque live-fire asador in Portland, Oregon. Includes a canvas hearth with wind-reactive flames and a hold-to-stoke interaction that unlocks an off-menu dish; four hand-drawn SVG dish illustrations and an illustrated dining room and map; a 40-dish menu with instant search (with Spanish synonym matching), category and dietary filters; a pickup-order basket with quantities, persistence, hours-aware pickup slots, validation and confirmation codes; a reservation flow with party/date/time logic, deterministic pseudo-random availability, closed Mondays and dated special closures, validation, persistence and two-step cancellation; live open-now status computed from the visitor's clock; opt-in Web Audio hearth crackle; mobile navigation; reduced-motion support. All storage access is guarded. Tested in Chromium via automation: menu, basket, reservation and navigation flows verified, no console errors. Known limitations: availability and codes are deterministic simulations (no backend); the animated fire loop pauses in fully backgrounded tabs by design and repaints on resize.
runs.title: Fuego Lento
runs.description: An independent restaurant, brought to life.

runs.notes: A self-contained canvas arcade flight game with procedural night-garden art, synthesized sound, escalating hazard density, pulse ability, keyboard/pointer/touch input, pause, and locally saved best score. Runs without external assets; browser storage and audio may be restricted by privacy settings.
runs.title: Noctiluca

runs.notes: Single-file 2D twin-stick gravity-well survival game (VORTEX). Vector-drawn canvas art, Web Audio synthesized SFX and music, particles, screen shake, hit-stop, slow-mo, dash, combo scoring, escalating endless waves, persistent best score via guarded localStorage. Known limitations: no external assets; touch and gamepad bindings implemented but not hardware-verified.
runs.title: Vortex

runs.notes: Aether Drift: neon top-down arena shooter/collector with waves, boss every 5th wave, phase (slow-mo+invuln) mechanic, entropy discharge via cores, procedural canvas art, synth audio+music, touch/gamepad support. Known limitations: music loop simple; no explicit victory state (endless survival).
runs.title: Aether Drift

runs.notes: A self-contained monochrome editorial field guide to the city after closing, with procedural canvas artwork, responsive layouts, and interactive field notes. No external assets or dependencies.
runs.title: Nocturne

runs.notes: NOCTURNE — a monochrome single-page atlas of the night train. Twelve real sleeper services (1883 to today) presented as a split-flap departures board, a hand-drawn Beck-style route diagram, per-service night sequences, and four short elegies. Static HTML/CSS/JS with no dependencies and no external requests; the split-flap engine is DOM + Web Animations, board clacks are synthesized with the Web Audio API (off by default), the diagram is hand-authored SVG. Fully responsive, keyboard accessible, motion respects prefers-reduced-motion, works from file:// and GitHub Pages subpaths. Known limitations: timetable times are indicative rather than authoritative (stated on the page) and the diagram is deliberately schematic, not to scale.
runs.title: Nocturne

runs.notes: Single-page monochrome interactive experience 'DIM — The Hour Between': scroll narrative on dusk and the hour between day and night, with a functional light-level dial, star/fog sky layers and a keeper's log. Hand-written HTML/CSS/vanilla JS and local SVG; no framework, no build step, no external assets. Known limitations: no-JS fallback leaves scroll-reveal content hidden until JavaScript runs; imagery is CSS/SVG only.
runs.title: Dim

runs.notes: Umbra is a single-page exhibition of twelve generative monochrome studies drawn live on Canvas 2D: interference rings, a halftone field, a flow field, ordered Bayer dithering, a harmonograph, phyllotaxis, marching-squares contours, Rule 30, stacked sine scans, a typographic density field, moire gratings and a halftoned sphere. Each plate is seeded and has two live parameters, a deep link, a PNG export and a pointer luminance readout; the method section adds an interactive tone-quantisation demo. Zero dependencies, no webfonts, no image files, no build step, relative paths throughout. Motion is capped at 30 fps, pauses off-screen and in hidden tabs, and defaults to paused under prefers-reduced-motion. Verified in Chromium at 1000x700: no console errors, only local asset requests, and every control, dialog, keyboard path and hash deep link exercised. The test browser could not produce animation frames (no visible window), so the twelve renderers were additionally run against a software rasteriser to confirm output and coverage, and responsive breakpoints were reviewed in CSS rather than emulated; Firefox and Safari were not available.
runs.title: Umbra

runs.notes: A complete monochrome fictional institution, the Bureau of Unseen Places. The site combines an editorial introduction, a live procedural survey-plate generator with four landforms and two atmospheric controls, a collected archive with accessible detail dialogs, SVG downloads, responsive layouts, and reduced-motion support. All artwork is generated inline in the browser; there are no external assets or dependencies. Known limitations: system fonts vary slightly between operating systems, and JavaScript is required for the plate generator and archive.
runs.title: The Bureau of Unseen Places

runs.notes: Two Tones is a single-file, strictly greyscale interactive atlas of dithering. It renders procedural sphere, ramp and relief sources on canvas through four 1-bit methods (threshold, Bayer ordered, Floyd–Steinberg, Atkinson), and includes a live studio, a pointer-driven hero light, an orbit toggle, PNG export, scroll progress and reduced-motion support. It uses no external files, fonts or libraries. Limitation: verified with static checks and a stubbed-DOM run only, not in a real browser, so visual layout and motion are untested; browsers without :has() show the selected-state styling less clearly.
runs.title: Two Tones

runs.notes: Standalone monochrome customs-clearance operations desk with local demo authentication, persistent declaration CRUD, search and filters, guarded status progression, indicative ZAR duty/VAT calculations, CSV export and printable text documents. No server or third-party integration; accounts and operational data are browser-local, and customs calculations are estimates requiring verification.
runs.title: Manifest
runs.description: A working customs and clearance workspace.

runs.notes: ClearDesk — a working SaaS for customs clearing agents: full clearance-entry pipeline with guarded status transitions (new → awaiting docs → lodged → customs query → assessed → duty paid → released → delivered → closed), an HS tariff schedule, duty/excise/VAT computation with pro-rata CIF allocation and FX conversion, per-mode document checklists that gate lodging, a disbursement ledger with aging buckets and payments, client statements, dashboard KPIs/reports, global search, keyboard shortcuts, CSV exports and printable duty-computation/entry sheets. Pure static product: index.html runs directly from file:// or any static host with zero install; data persists in localStorage (every access wrapped in try/catch with an in-memory fallback and warning banner). Auth is local (salted SHA-256), seed data is generated relative to the current date, and the domain-logic test suite can be run from Settings → Diagnostics (also 'node assets/core.test.js'). Demo credentials are shown on the sign-in screen: clara.otien@atlasfreight.app / demo1234 (manager) and james.mwangi@atlasfreight.app / demo1234 (clerk). Known limitations: single-browser storage, illustrative tariff rates, no real customs-authority or payment integration, local-only auth.
runs.title: ClearDesk
runs.description: A working customs and clearance workspace.

runs.notes: ClearLane is a client-side SaaS prototype for customs clearing agents: shipment CRUD with domain validation, customs value and duty/tax calculations, document generation (commercial invoice, packing list, customs entry export) and a clearance status workflow. Ships as a static build with localStorage persistence and seeded demo data. Known limitations: no server-side backend or real auth provider, demo-grade password hashing, illustrative duty rate table only, no live customs API integration.
runs.title: ClearLane
runs.description: A working customs and clearance workspace.

runs.notes: Clearway is a local-first customs clearance desk for clearing agents: job files, client records, live duty/MPF/HMF estimates, document control, status workflow, entry worksheets, printable entry summaries, CSV exports, and dashboard/report analytics. It runs with no server, build step, API keys, or external accounts; state persists in localStorage and is seeded with a 14-job demo workspace (ops@clearway.co / clearway123). Known limitations: browser-local data only with no sync or server-side auth; passwords are salted and hashed locally but this is not an enterprise identity system; duty/MPF/HMF figures are seeded operational estimates, not a live tariff database or legal filing; document attachments are not stored, only document metadata and references; no customs authority or broker network integration.
runs.title: Clearway
runs.description: A working customs and clearance workspace.

runs.notes: Declarant is a local-first customs clearing workspace for a Mombasa freight desk. It covers intake, document checklists with lodgement gates, pro-rata CIF allocation, duty/excise/VAT/levy computation, assessments, customs queries, release and delivery, disbursement aging, client statements, CSV exports, print documents and role-based demo accounts. Runs directly from index.html with seeded data and localStorage persistence; no server, build step or external services. Limitations: tariff rates and the demo accounts are illustrative and not a substitute for current authority tariffs or real authentication; data is confined to one browser profile; CSV and print output are the only integrations; the bundled test suite covers core calculations, document gating, aging and storage serialisation, not browser rendering.
runs.title: Declarant
runs.description: A working customs and clearance workspace.

runs.notes: Interactive four-stroke spark-ignition engine cutaway with thermodynamic cycle, crank-slider kinematics, cam-driven valves, spark ignition, particle flow, live pressure/torque/valve-lift graphs, what-if failures and parameters, exploded view, sound and hidden oil-jet detail. Single-file canvas app; reduced-motion and touch/keyboard supported. Thermodynamics uses a simplified filling-and-emptying model; values are physically plausible but not CFD-grade.
runs.title: Four-Stroke Engine

runs.notes: Lantern Drift: a third-person floating-island platformer where a paper-lantern spirit collects memory-orbs and evades shadow wraiths across five escalating realms. Procedural geometry, synthesized Web Audio music and SFX, bloom postprocessing, particles, pointer-lock mouse look, touch and gamepad support, pause, high score via localStorage. Known limitations: traversal relies on procedural island chains that are usually but not always cleanly jumpable; bloom loads asynchronously from CDN.
runs.title: Lantern Drift

runs.notes: Komorebi, a Japanese-Danish open-fire restaurant in Copenhagen. Single-file site with full 33-item menu, instant search and dietary/category filters, reservation flow with calendar and slot logic, takeaway basket with localStorage persistence and checkout, real-time open/closed status from opening hours, mobile navigation, Web Audio ambient toggle, canvas hero/story/gallery illustrations, and a hidden chef's dish easter egg. No external assets beyond Google Fonts.
runs.title: Komorebi
runs.description: An independent restaurant, brought to life.

runs.notes: Strata is an offline, dependency-free terrain instrument with four original procedural landforms, editable seeded geometry, local collections, and PNG and OBJ export. No runtime model identifier was exposed. Saved collections are browser-local; when persistent storage is unavailable, they last for the current session only.
runs.title: Strata / Terrain Studio

runs.notes: Static, single-entry-point editorial site for the fictional monthly publication FOLD. Hero with a hand-drawn folded-sheet animation, a story list using details accordions with scroll-reveal, an About section with a hand-drawn typewriter illustration, and a Contact section with a mailto address and CTA. All imagery is hand-drawn SVG (hero sheets, per-story glyphs, typewriter); colours are strictly greyscale; favicon is assets/favicon.svg. A small inline script adds scroll reveal with prefers-reduced-motion support. Works from file:// and GitHub Pages via relative paths.
runs.title: Fold

runs.notes: STATIC — an interactive monochrome meditation on electromagnetic noise, dead air, and the space between stations. Built with vanilla HTML/CSS/JS and 2D canvas. No external dependencies, no frameworks, no image assets. Features seven generative canvas studies, a working Web Audio radio tuner, keyboard navigation, reduced-motion support, and screen-reader accessible copy. Model identity not exposed by runtime, so 'unknown-model' is used per instructions.
runs.title: Static

runs.notes: Silent Press: a static, strictly monochrome editorial site with a seeded SVG poster generator, six selectable editions, live proofing, SVG download and shareable settings links. All artwork is drawn in code; there are no external assets or dependencies. Model identity was confirmed by the operator as Hy4 Flash. Requires JavaScript for the generator and interactive controls; the written content remains readable without it.
runs.title: Silent Press

runs.notes: A standalone, strictly monochrome editorial website about the tones between black and white, with a pointer-reactive Canvas field, a luminance-matching instrument, six procedurally drawn plates, a selectable grey register, inverted theme, print styles and reduced-motion support. Model identity was confirmed by the operator as Hy4. No external assets, fonts, libraries or network calls; all imagery is SVG or Canvas. Known limitation: the interactive instruments require JavaScript, although the editorial text and initial captions remain in the HTML.
runs.title: The Grey Matter

runs.notes: LUMEN: a first-person descent into a bioluminescent cave system. Collect 8 crystals, avoid 8 patrolling Shades, stun them with a resonance pulse. Features pointer-lock FPS controls with AABB collision, sprint/stamina, health pickups, positional Web Audio, bloom post-processing, adaptive quality, gamepad and touch support, settings persistence, and win/lose/restart loop. Known limitations: requires network for Three.js CDN; touch controls are basic; no save of in-progress run beyond best time.

runs.notes: Aether Drift: neon twin-stick survival with seeded runs, daily seed, run modifiers, power-ups, combos/graze, waves and bosses, meta upgrades, local leaderboard, ghost replay of best run, touch and gamepad support. runs.title: Aether Drift

runs.notes: Aether OS: a single-file browser desktop with invented visual language, procedural wallpapers, synthesized sound, a real window manager, persisted virtual filesystem, and 10 apps (Files, Terminal, Editor, Paint, Music, Calendar, Browser, Monitor, Settings, Calculator). Includes lock screen, launcher with live search, notifications, alt-tab, context menus, and keyboard shortcuts. Terminal supports pipes, redirection, history, and tab completion.
